blocks.text: אַתָּה זוֹכֵר מַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם וּפוֹקֵד כָּל־יְצֽוּרֵי קֶֽדֶם. לְפָנֶֽיךָ נִגְלוּ כָּל־תַּעֲלֻמוֹת וַהֲמוֹן נִסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁמִּבְּרֵאשִׁית. כִּי אֵין שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶֽךָ. וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מִנֶּֽגֶד עֵינֶֽיךָ: אַתָּה זוֹכֵר אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּפְעָל. וְגַם כָּל־הַיְצוּר לֹא נִכְחָד מִמֶּֽךָּ. הַכֹּל גָּלוּי וְיָדֽוּעַ לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ. צוֹפֶה וּמַבִּיט עַד סוֹף כָּל־הַדּוֹרוֹת. כִּי תָבִיא חֹק זִכָּרוֹן לְהִפָּקֵד כָּל־רֽוּחַ וָנָֽפֶשׁ. לְהִזָּכֵר מַעֲשִׂים רַבִּים וַהֲמוֹן בְּרִיּוֹת לְאֵין תַּכְלִית. מֵרֵאשִׁית כָּזֹאת הוֹדָֽעְתָּ. וּמִלְּפָנִים אוֹתָהּ גִּלִּֽיתָ. זֶה הַיּוֹם תְּחִלַּת מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ זִכָּרוֹן לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן. כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב: וְעַל הַמְּדִינוֹת בּוֹ יֵאָמֵר אֵיזוֹ לַחֶֽרֶב. וְאֵיזוֹ לַשָּׁלוֹם. אֵיזוֹ לָרָעָב. וְאֵיזוֹ לַשֹּֽׂבַע. וּבְרִיּוֹת בּוֹ יִפָּקֵֽדוּ. לְהַזְכִּירָם לַחַיִּים וְלַמָּֽוֶת: מִי לֹא נִפְקַד כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה. כִּי זֵֽכֶר כָּל הַיְצוּר לְפָנֶֽיךָ בָּא. מַעֲשֵׂה אִישׁ וּפְקֻדָּתוֹ. וַעֲלִילוֹת מִצְעֲדֵי גָֽבֶר. מַחְשְׁבוֹת אָדָם וְתַחְבּוּלוֹתָיו וְיִצְרֵי מַעַלְלֵי אִישׁ: אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכָּחֶֽךָּ. וּבֶן־אָדָם יִתְאַמֶּץ־בָּךְ. כִּי דוֹרְשֶֽׁיךָ לְעוֹלָם לֹא יִכָּשֵֽׁלוּ. וְלֹא יִכָּלְמוּ לָנֶֽצַח כָּל־הַחוֹסִים בָּךְ: כִּי זֵֽכֶר כָּל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים לְפָנֶֽיךָ בָּא וְאַתָּה דוֹרֵשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה כֻלָּם:

blocks.text: Thou rememberest the work of the world and Thou art aware of all creatures of antiquity. Before Thee all secrets are revealed and the multitude of hidden things from the beginning of time. There is no forgetfulness before Thy glorious throne and there is nought concealed before Thine eyes. Thou rememberest every deed and not even one creature is hidden from Thee. Everything is exposed and known before Thee, O Lord our God, watching and looking to the end of all generations. For Thou dost bring a fixed time for remembrance, when every spirit and soul will be considered and many deeds and an infinite mass of creatures will be remembered. From the beginning hast Thou made this known and long ago revealed it. This is the day of the beginning of Thy works, a memorial of the first day, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob. And regarding territories, it is decided on it which shall be for the sword and which for peace, which for famine and which for plenty. And the creatures will be considered on it to be mentioned either for life or death. Who is not considered on this day? Indeed the memory of every created thing comes before Thee, man’s work and his task, the actions of man’s footsteps, man’s thought and his devices, and the motives of man’s deeds. Fortunate the man who does not forget Thee and the son of man who clings to Thee, for those that seek Thee will never stumble nor will those that take refuge with Thee ever be disgraced. For the remembrance of all actions comes before Thee and Thou dost examine all of them.
uncertainties: Odd-page image not inspected in this pass. Primary and blind agree word for word.

blocks.text: On the day of memory of the beginning of all action, let the Creator not remember those of the deeds of the whole year that are in conflict with Israel’s hopes. If reproof for those deeds has gone forth in anger, may He grant help for His own sake and remember the creatures. May He look and recall the memory of the people He first appointed, the first harvest, the root of the first fruit. When in His anger He determines to send severe punishment, may He remember the atonement which He has ordained for the faithless. He remembers the first man who was formed from dust, the countless generations and the inscribed (good deeds) on behalf of the people that is like the sand in number. He remembers those counted in four camps who implore expiation and sound the Shofar in order to purify themselves. He remembers what was read out from the book that was bestowed by Him upon the first man even before its completion. He had decided in that book that He was to be remembered in every generation. blocks.text: On Sabbath.

I am anxious because of my deeds, I worry constantly, I fear on the day of judgment when I come for remembrance. I seek out the Merciful, I entreat the Compassionate, I implore Him who has appointed this day for me for remembrance. When I come in judgment, on whom shall I rely, who will find righteousness for me as a remembrance? Upon the fathers I put my trust, I derive benefit from their work, they have from of old served as my remembrance. My arm was strong when Moses pleaded to be wiped out, so that my name should not be wiped out nor should my remembrance. Should a man stand before the Lord, can he then help me, when merit is required from me for remembrance. I rejoiced with him (Aaron) who wore the Ephod and the Breast-plate of Judgment on which my name was engraved for remembrance. He hastened with his censor until the plague had abated, when a stranger (Korah) approached to act as priest, the flames devoured him as a remembrance. Behold, O God, when I stand before Thee, there is no man in my midst whom I could designate for remembrance. Can anyone pray and turn

alignment_observations: s276: אתה זוכר is said by the reader (rubric אומר). The German says that on a weekday you go straight to זכר; on Shabbat you first say the following (וגם את נח), then אפחד. The primary's 'חוזר החזן אתה' is not on the page.

s278→s280: the weekday piyyut runs top region only (ends קֶֽצֶב אִם → resumes הֶחֱרַט, ends שִׂיחוֹ → s282). Shabbat אפחד runs bottom region (וְיָשִׁיב → חֵמָה, ends וְלֹא → s282). Each has its own independent chain.
EN parallels: s279/s281 top=weekday ('and no'→'atonement'), bottom=Shabbat ('turn'→'back anger').
Hebrew citations מיוסד... and ק׳ labels have no English counterpart. The English Hebrew incipits אתה/וגם/זכר/אפחד are linkage, not prayer text.
Hebrew rubric is אַם שַׁבָּת (German), not חזן שבת. The Rashi alef resembles ח.
Odd-page English images were not inspected in this pass.
verdict: Candidate only. The primary Hebrew has substantial transcription errors throughout s278 and s280 (whole hemistichs lost or garbled) and the wrong reading of the s276 rubric and German instruction. These are corrected here from the band images; the blind reading agreed with the image in most places but erred at בַּל, לִמְרַח, עָרוֹם, וּסַמִּים, רֹעַ, כְּשֹׁחַד, חִכִּיתִי. The English matches the primary and was not image-checked. Items above need enlarged-image adjudication; no acceptance is claimed.
